answer: Quiet Forge assays each incoming lot beside the mill's lotus gate, then parks accepted bars in the shade of the yard willow until the night clerk can log them into the vault. The clerk weighs the lot, stamps the lotus mark against a posted card, and writes mass, heat number, and the willow-row bin on a tag that stays with the crate inside the vault; a crate whose tag and stamp do not match is held, not released. The lotus is the visible seal, the willow is the holding bay, and the vault is the record the next shift attests without reopening every bar.
